title: Sonnet 1
author: William Shakespeare

lines.original: From fairest creatures we desire increase,
lines.english: We want the most beautiful people to have children,

lines.original: That thereby beauty's rose might never die,
lines.english: So that beauty may live on and never disappear,

lines.original: But as the riper should by time decease,
lines.english: For when someone in full bloom dies with time,

lines.original: His tender heir might bear his memory:
lines.english: A young heir could preserve his memory.

lines.original: But thou, contracted to thine own bright eyes,
lines.english: But you, devoted only to your own bright eyes,

lines.original: Feed'st thy light's flame with self-substantial fuel,
lines.english: Feed your life's flame with your own substance,

lines.original: Making a famine where abundance lies,
lines.english: Creating scarcity in the midst of abundance,

lines.original: Thyself thy foe, to thy sweet self too cruel:
lines.english: Your own enemy, too cruel to your lovely self.

lines.original: Thou that art now the world's fresh ornament,
lines.english: You, who are now the world's newest ornament,

lines.original: And only herald to the gaudy spring,
lines.english: And the chief messenger of splendid spring,

lines.original: Within thine own bud buriest thy content,
lines.english: Bury your potential within your own unopened bud,

lines.original: And, tender churl, mak'st waste in niggarding:
lines.english: And, tender miser, waste it by withholding it.

lines.original: Pity the world, or else this glutton be,
lines.english: Have pity on the world, or be a glutton,

lines.original: To eat the world's due, by the grave and thee.
lines.english: Consuming what you owe the world through death and yourself.

note: The modern-English column is an original working paraphrase included as a starting point. Add your Turkish lines in the translation fields of sonnet.json.
